sections.heading: About Lord Ayyappa
sections.content: Lord Ayyappa, also known as Dharma Sastha, is a Hindu deity who is the son of Harihara (Vishnu and Shiva). He is particularly worshipped in Kerala and is the presiding deity of the famous Sabarimala temple. Ayyappa is depicted as a celibate yogi, and devotees observe strict penance before visiting the temple.

sections.heading: Sabarimala Pilgrimage
sections.content: The Sabarimala pilgrimage is one of the largest annual pilgrimages in the world. Devotees undertake a 41-day vratham (penance) wearing black/blue clothes, practicing celibacy, and following a vegetarian diet. The pilgrimage season culminates during the Makaravilakku festival.

sections.heading: Vratham and Devotion
sections.content: During the 41-day vratham, devotees wake up early, take bath twice daily, visit temples regularly, abstain from intoxicants, practice celibacy, and chant 'Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa'. This spiritual discipline purifies the mind and body.

sections.heading: Makaravilakku
sections.content: Makaravilakku is the divine light that appears on the hills of Sabarimala on Makara Sankranti (January 14/15). Millions of devotees witness this celestial phenomenon, which is considered highly auspicious and marks the culmination of the pilgrimage season.
